observations.content:
Summary: The capital city of Australia is Canberra. The sources confirm that Canberra is the capital city of Australia and is located in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT). It was chosen as the capital in 1908 and formally named in 1913. Canberra is also described as the largest inland city in Australia and the eighth-largest city by population.

[1] Canberra - Wikipedia
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra
    Canberra (/ˈkænbrə/ ⓘ KAN-brə; Ngunawal: Kanbarra) is the capital city of Australia and the largest population centre in the Australian Capital Territory. With an estimated population of 484,630 as of 2025, Canberra is Australia's largest inland city and the eighth-largest Australian city by population. The city occupies most of the northern quadrant of the Australian Capital Territory, and its urban sprawl borders the state of New South Wales to the northwest, northeast and southeast. The [...] surviving landmarks such as St John's Anglican Church and Blundells Cottage. On 1 January 1901, federation of the colonies of Australia was achieved. The capital city was founded and formally named as Canberra in 1913. Unusual among Australian cities, it is an entirely planned city, grounded in a design by American architects Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin.     In 1908, the Canberra-Yass district was chosen as the capital site. In 1911, the federal government began acquiring land for the city, which has remained under government ownership. Construction was interrupted by World War I but resumed afterward, and the first Parliament House opened in 1927, when the population neared 6,000. Today, the ACT is home to Canberra, the national capital, and numerous conservation areas.

## Full article

The Australian Capital Territory (ACT) is a territory between Sydney and Melbourne in south-east Australia that is home to the country's capital city, Canberra, which is also its largest inland city. Canberra was selected as the country's capital city in 1908 and it is located at the northern end of the ACT. The total area of the ACT measures 2,358 square kilometres (910 square miles).
